# Background & aims

1.  

## Literature

- Cornwell & Ackerly 2009
- Ogle 2014 - wood density
- Fischer et al 2025 (in review) - Global Wood Density Database. partition variance at different levels of biological organisation and with and quantify correlations with climate variables. They fit exactly the same structure for the mixed effect model that I ended up using, including the two climate variables, the average species value and the centered deviation from the average. Reassuring that they converged on the same approach. They cite an Gelman reference (guru statistician) where they recommend this approach for LMMs when "Predictors and Group Effects Correlate"  https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.1010095



# Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(easystats)
library(broom.mixed)
library(arrow)
library(modelbased)
library(tmbstan)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r}
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
```

```{r}
data_traits_climate <-
  arrow::read_parquet("data-processed/data_traits_climate.parquet")
```

```{r}
data_traits_climate |>
  pull(taxon_name) |>
  unique() |> 
  length()
```

```{r}
data_traits_climate <- data_traits_climate |>
select(decimal_longitude:life_stage, growth_form_simpler, life_history, woody) |>
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C",(-8 - value) / (1+(value/1000)), value)) %>% 
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log(annual_precipitation),
    log_value = log(value)
  ) |>
  # Let's also collect the mean rainfall and temp for each species, and devitations of each from their respective mean
  group_by(taxon_name, cell) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$log_annual_precipitation[1]),
    average_temperature_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$average_temperature[1])
  ) |>
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(log_annual_precipitation_cell),
    # log_annual_precipitation_c = log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    average_temperature_mn = mean(average_temperature_cell)
    # ,
    # average_temperature_c = average_temperature - average_temperature_mn
  ) |>
  unnest(data) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(log_annual_precipitation_c = log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    average_temperature_c = average_temperature - average_temperature_mn) |>
  # # add a site index, based on unqiue lat, longley
  # mutate(site_id = paste(decimal_longitude, decimal_latitude, sep= "-")) |>
  #filter out species that have only cell occurrence
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(ncell = length(unique((cell)))) |> 
  ungroup() |>
  filter(ncell > 1)

# data_traits_climate_woody <- data_traits_climate |>
#   filter(woody == "woody")
```

# Comapring two methods: Straight Mixed effects models vs Cornwell-Ackerly Method

Let's try within species for LMA

```{r}
trait <- "leaf_mass_per_area"

data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
  filter(trait_name == trait)

# model across species means
fit0 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c, data = data_model)
fit1 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c + (1 | taxon_name), data = data_model)
fit2 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name), data = data_model)

# check support for random intercepts and slopes -- strong
anova(fit0, fit1, fit2)
```

Let's now extract fitted values and plot it. 

We want a plot with species means and global model added, so I'm going to extract several predicted values then join

```{r}
# overall fitted - with REs
data_fit2_re <- estimate_expectation(fit2) |>
  as_tibble()

# Global prediction - change in species mean trait with climate
data_fit2_global <- estimate_means(fit2, by = "log_annual_precipitation_mn") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  # change variable names so these will plot ok
  select(log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn, log_value = Mean) |>
  # backtransform so we can plot on raw scale
  mutate(
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    value = exp(log_value),
    # need a taxon name for plotting
    taxon_name = "global average"
  )

# caluclate species means by removing devistations from center
data_fit2_mn <- estimate_expectation(fit2,
  data = data_fit2_re |> mutate(log_annual_precipitation_c = 0) |> select(-Predicted) |> distinct()
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  distinct()

# combine
data_fit2 <-
  data_fit2_re |>
  rename(log_value = Predicted) |>
  select(-SE, -Residuals) |>
  left_join(
    by = c("log_annual_precipitation_mn", "taxon_name"),
    data_fit2_mn |> select(log_annual_precipitation_mn, taxon_name, log_value_mn = Predicted)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c,
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    annual_precipitation_mn = exp(log_annual_precipitation_mn),
    value = exp(log_value),
    value_mn = exp(log_value_mn),
  )
set.seed(123)
# Choose a subset of taxa to plot. We'll choose randomly, but restrict to those with multiple sites and records
taxa <- data_model |>
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  summarise(
    # how many observations for that taxon
    n = n(),
    # how many distinct sites # TODO: cell ID
    n_sites = n_distinct(annual_precipitation)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(n > 4, n_sites > 2) |>
  pull(taxon_name) |>
  unique() |>
  sample(15)

data_model_taxa <- data_model |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

data_fit2_taxa <- data_fit2 |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

p_fit <-
  data_fit2 |>
  ggplot(aes(annual_precipitation, value, group = taxon_name)) +
  # raw data
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, col = "grey", data = data_model, stroke = 0) +
  # fitted lines
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, col = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  # highlight certain species
  geom_point(aes(group = taxon2), col = "orange", show.legend = FALSE, data = data_model_taxa, size = 0.9, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(group = taxon2), col = "#d95f02", alpha = 1, show.legend = FALSE, data = data_fit2_taxa) +
  # global line
  geom_line(data = data_fit2_global, col = "red") +
  # species centers
  geom_point(aes(x = annual_precipitation_mn, y = value_mn, group = taxon2), col = "red", alpha = 1, size = 0.9,stroke = 0, data = data_fit2_taxa) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = trait, x = "annual rainfall") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~taxon2)

ggsave("outputs/lma_species_panel_species.png", p_fit)
```

```{r}
# model across species means
parameters::parameters(fit2)
```

Plot random slopes. These are deviations from the average species response, which is negative. They should be centred around zero, which they are. 

```{r}
species_slopes_c <-
  broom.mixed::tidy(fit2, effects = "ran_vals") |>
  filter(term == "log_annual_precipitation_c") |>
  select(level, estimate) |>
  rename(taxon_name = level, slope_c = estimate)

# Range of within species slopes
stats::quantile(species_slopes_c$slope_c, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.9))

ggplot(species_slopes_c, aes(slope_c)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

# Repeat for multiple traits

Let's now wrap into functions and repeat 

```{r}
source("R/fit_model_1D.R")

traits <- c(
  "leaf_mass_per_area", "leaf_area",
  "leaf_N_per_area", "leaf_P_per_area",
  "wood_density"
)

fits <- list()

climates <- c("log_annual_precipitation","average_temperature")

for (trait in traits) {
  for (climate in climates) {

  cat(trait, ":  ")
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)
  fits[[trait]] <- fit_model_1D(data_model, seed = 123, ind_variable= climate)
  ggsave(sprintf("outputs/%s_species_panel.png", paste0(trait,"_",climate)), fits[[trait]]$plot_fitted)
  }
}
```

Accessing fitted objects for more analysis

```{r}
names(fits)
names(fits[["leaf_mass_per_area"]])

parameters(fits[["leaf_mass_per_area"]][["fit"]])

parameters(fits[["wood_density"]][["fit"]])
```

# Two environmental parameters

Interaction model doesn't appear to be possible for leaf mass per area at least

```{r}
fit3 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c + average_temperature_mn + average_temperature_c + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name) + (average_temperature_c | taxon_name), data = data_model)

fit4 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn*average_temperature_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c*average_temperature_c + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name)+ (average_temperature_c | taxon_name) + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name)+ (log_annual_precipitation_c:average_temperature_c | taxon_name), data = data_model)
```

# Fitting Bayesian models of 2d models for relative contribution question

```{r}
source("R/fit_model2d_bayesian.R")

traits <- data_traits_climate$trait_name %>% unique()
traits <- traits[c(1,4,5,7,9)]
# traits <- traits[4:5]
options(mc.cores = 4)
fits_bayesian <- list()

for (trait in traits) {
  cat(trait, ":  ")
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)
  fits_bayesian[[trait]] <- fit_model2d_bayesian(data_model)
}
```

```{r}
traits <- unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name)
traits <- traits[c(1:5,7,9)]
fits_bayesian <- list()
posterior_matrix_in <- list()

for (trait in traits) {
  fits_bayesian[[trait]] <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/",trait,".RDS"))
  
  posterior_matrix_in[[trait]] <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(fits_bayesian[[trait]][[2]])%>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(prec_mn = 'beta[2]', prec_c = 'beta[3]', temp_mn = 'beta[4]',temp_c = 'beta[5]') %>%
  mutate(trait_name = trait)
}

posterior_matrix_in %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    mutate(ratio_prec = prec_c/prec_mn) %>%
    select(-contains("temp")) |>
    # mutate(ratio_temp = temp_c/temp_mn)%>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -c(trait_name), names_to = "climate")%>%
    mutate(climate = factor(climate, levels = c("ratio_prec", "prec_mn","prec_c"), labels = c(bquote(Ratio), bquote(B[2[Prec]]), bquote(B[1[Prec]])))) |>
    mutate(trait_name = factor(trait_name, levels = c("huber_value", "leaf_area","leaf_delta13C","leaf_mass_per_area","leaf_N_per_area","leaf_P_per_area","wood_density"), labels = c("SA:LA",bquote(Leaf~area), bquote(Leaf~delta^13*C),"LMA",bquote(Leaf~N[area]),bquote(Leaf~P[area]),bquote(Wood~density)))) %>% group_by(trait_name, climate) %>% summarise(median = median(value), lower_quant = quantile(value, 0.05), upper_quant = quantile(value, 0.95)) -> quants





posterior_matrix_in %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(ratio_prec = prec_c/prec_mn) %>%
  select(-contains("temp")) |>
  # mutate(ratio_temp = temp_c/temp_mn)%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(trait_name), names_to = "climate")%>%
  mutate(climate = factor(climate, levels = c("ratio_prec", "prec_mn","prec_c"), labels = c(bquote(Ratio), bquote(B[2[Prec]]), bquote(B[1[Prec]])))) |>
  mutate(trait_name = factor(trait_name, levels = c("huber_value", "leaf_area","leaf_delta13C","leaf_mass_per_area","leaf_N_per_area","leaf_P_per_area","wood_density"), labels = c("SA:LA",bquote(Leaf~area), bquote(Leaf~delta^13*C),"LMA",bquote(Leaf~N[area]),bquote(Leaf~P[area]),bquote(Wood~density)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = as.numeric(value), y = climate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(aes(colour = climate, group = climate, fill = climate),alpha=0.5,scale = 0.5,size = 1)+
  geom_segment(data = quants, aes(y = climate, yend = climate, x = lower_quant, xend = upper_quant), size = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = quants, aes(y = climate, x = median), size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~trait_name, scales = "free_x", labeller = label_parsed, ncol = 2) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        # axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        strip.border = element_rect(color = NA),
        legend.position = "none",
          text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) parse(text = x)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("green","orange","purple"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green","orange","purple"))

ggsave("rel_intra_inter_prec.png", height = 7)
```

```{r}
source("R/fit_model2d_3panel_PFT.R")

traits <- unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name)

traits <- traits[-c(6,8,10)]
fit_model2d_3panelPFT_out <- list()

for (trait in traits) {
  cat(trait, ":  ")
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(growth_form_simpler != "primitive") |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)
  fit_model2d_3panelPFT_out[[trait]] <- fit_model2d_3panel_PFT(data_model, ind_variable = "log_annual_precipitation")
}

patchwork::wrap_plots(fit_model2d_3panelPFT_out, ncol = 1, guides = "collect", tag = "new") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")

ggsave("fit_model2d_3panel_precipitation2.png", height = 18, width = 10)
```
